quote: And I'm just gonna take a quick look at your roof on Google Maps. And just out of curiosity, we've got you interested in solar.
stewart_read: Rep runs the standard roof-check step from the new-install script without first confirming whether the customer already has solar — this is the moment a quick 'do you currently have solar panels installed?' verify question would have surfaced the DQ before the Google Maps step.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to ask 'do you already have solar on the home?' as an early verify question before running the visual roof check, so existing-system cases are caught in seconds rather than via surprise during the Maps lookup.

quote: Were you looking into getting additional panels or a backup battery for your home?
stewart_read: Rep correctly identifies existing panels on Google Maps and pivots to the orphaned-flow branch, but does so without first asking the schema's orphaned_flow lead questions (own vs. lease, which company, is it working) in sequence — he improvises the branch reactively.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may be intentionally leading with an upsell frame (battery/additional panels) to keep the call value-positive before diagnosing the system's status, rather than opening with 'is your system working?' which risks an immediate DQ-and-hangup.
coaching_implication: Walk through orphaned_flow's ordered questions (ownership type, company, panel size, working status) so the rep has a structured branch instead of guessing the reason for interest.

stewart_read: Customer names the installer as 'Sun City,' which the rep (at 02:01) interprets as 'SolarCity' — a hard-DQ company per dq_rules. This is a diarization-sensitive moment; the correction itself is reasonable rep behavior given likely mispronunciation, but it is the pivotal DQ trigger.
coaching_implication: No coaching action needed on the interpretation itself — flag for the manager only as the exact point the DQ is confirmed, for QA purposes.

quote: to get those back going again, you'd have to contact SolarCity, and they they would be able to help you with that. But I so I I'm not able to help get those working again.
stewart_read: Rep gives an honest, correct answer instead of overselling a fix Ion cannot provide — this is the right procedural move on a hard-DQ existing-broken-system scenario and should be reinforced as good practice.
coaching_implication: Reinforce this as the correct model: when a system is broken and installed by another company, tell the customer plainly Ion can't service it, then check for any adjacent legitimate offer.

quote: But if you were wanting to get, like, a backup battery or additional panels, I can help you with getting that.
stewart_read: Rep attempts a legitimate adjacent-sale pivot (battery/additional panels) after correctly disqualifying the broken-system repair ask. The customer's immediate 'No. Thank you' at 02:37 shows this pivot did not land — the offer arrived without any bridge (no acknowledgment of the inconvenience of a broken system, no curiosity hook) and reads as a generic upsell tacked onto a DQ rather than a considered cross-sell.
alternative_hypothesis: A charitable read would call this a reasonable exploratory move given the schema allows battery/additional-panel sales into existing-solar homes — but the immediate flat decline and lack of any framing beyond the bare question suggests execution was weak, not just unlucky timing.
coaching_implication: When pivoting to an adjacent sale after a DQ, acknowledge the customer's frustration with the broken system first, then frame the battery/panel option as solving a related pain point rather than asking a flat either/or question.

stewart_read: Call ends on the customer's decline with no attempt at a soft close, no offer to follow up if the SolarCity situation changes, and no button-up mechanics — the call simply stops.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: since this is a hard DQ (broken system with another company) and the customer declined the only viable offer, there may be nothing left to close — persisting further could read as pushy on a clearly disqualified lead.
coaching_implication: Even on a DQ, a brief close ('if that ever changes or you want a battery down the line, feel free to reach out') costs nothing and leaves the door open — coach the rep to end DQ calls with a small forward-looking line rather than just 'Okay.'
